translation: When the spleen and stomach are vacuous, [the person] is lethargic and loves recumbence, and cannot gather the four limbs. When the season happens to be autumn-dryness carrying out its order, and the dampness-heat has retreated a little, [there may be] heaviness of the body, aching of the joints, dry mouth and dry tongue, food and drink without flavor, irregularities in the stool, frequent urination, no desire for food, indigestion of food, and, together, the appearance of lung disease: 洒淅 aversion to cold (chilly aversion to cold)... actually "洒淅惡寒" chills and shivering with aversion to cold, 慘慘不樂 gloomy and joyless; the complexion is harsh and not harmonious — all because the yang qi does not stretch forth. One should raise yang and augment qi; I name it Sheng Yang Yi Wei Tang (Raise-Yang Augment-Stomach Decoction).
